text: The case record reads the deviation section of a case on GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations, one hop and inside a 2 s budget, and the read answers every deviation of the case, open and cleared.
why: The Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations (POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}) and no read, while legacy RWB-E2-015 section 12 calls DeviationQuery.forCase on the case record path with a 2 s timeout (NFR-008) and RWB-P3-E2015-CON expects a deviation view the record composes; no source publishes a read of the section.
read: Context pack S8 ownership rows (REST operations provided: 2); legacy RWB-E2-015 sections 4, 11, 12; TSD S8 T3.1, T-A.1; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R9
applied_in: RWB-S8-E2015-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 7 AC1 and AC7, 12.1, 12.8 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-deviation owner, before RWB-P3-E2015-CON is tagged
impact: One read operation is published on the service base; if the Ownership Map is not amended, the operation has no catalogue row and the gap is reported at wave 2 exit

text: The deviation view the case record consumes is named here as deviationId, caseId, deviationCode, deviationLabel, state, raisedAt, handlerUserId, pausedState, contactStop, clearedAt, outcome, outcomeLabel, decisionRecordId, slaDueAt and slaBreached, with the case-level openCount, anyOpen, contactStopActive and stageClockPausedSince beside it.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-015 section 11 names seven deviation columns read through the interface and section 12 names the Case and Timer fields, while no source publishes the field names of the deviation view that RWB-P3-E2015-CON carries; the names are fixed here so the contract and its fake can be built.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-015 sections 11 and 12, AC2, AC5 and AC7; TSD S8 T3.1; FSD S8 A2.8.3.2
applied_in: RWB-S8-E2015-APP sections 3, 7 AC1 to AC5, 12.1 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case contract owner, when RWB-P3-E2015-CON is reviewed
impact: A field rename after the contract is tagged changes this read and the record together; no business value changes

text: A case this service holds no deviation for is answered with an empty deviations list, openCount 0 and anyOpen false, with 200, and not with a 404.
why: The case row is rwb-case's row and this service holds no copy of it (DP-01), so it cannot confirm the existence of a case; a 404 would also claim a scope decision that belongs to rwb-access and rwb-case.
read: Context pack S8 ownership rows; TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01; legacy RWB-E2-015 section 10
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-deviation owner
impact: The record shows a case with no deviation as clear rather than as an error; a wrong case reference still fails on the case answer of rwb-case

text: The label of a deviation code and the label of an outcome are read on the reference-data contract of rwb-case at the version in force; only the label of X3, Deceased customer, is published for this slice, an outcome is shown as its LOV-DEV-OUTCOME value when it has no label, and a code with no label is shown as its code with the marker unmapped.
why: TSD S8 T3.2 prints LOV-DEVIATION as the seven bare codes and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME as RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED, while legacy AC2 needs the label Deceased customer for X3 on the record; no source prints the other labels or a field ID for a label, and the labels must not be typed in code (FSD S8 BR-S8-001).
read: TSD S8 T3.2; FSD S8 A2.8.3.2 and BR-S8-001; legacy RWB-E2-015 AC2 and AC7
applied_in: RWB-S8-E2015-APP sections 4 step 5, 7 AC1, 8 BR5, 11, 12.2 and 13
confirm: The rwb-case reference-data owner and the business analyst of S8
impact: A missing label leaves the record readable with the code; a wrong label is a data correction, not a release

text: The deviation service level is a reference-data row read at the version in force, its published value is 10 working days from the Architecture v5 slide 8 note, and R-DEV-20 keeps the deviation in DEV_WITH_OWNER when it breaches; the escalation target role and the codes R-DEV-20 covers are not published, no escalation task is raised in rwb-case by this slice, and the escalation is recorded in the service's local decision record instead.
why: FSD S8 A2.1.1 sets the target with DL22 and the slide 8 note says the deviation escalates if it is not resolved in 10 working days, while TSD S8 T4 prints R-DEV-20 without the codes it covers or the role it escalates to; the parameter contract of DP-06 is not in this story's pattern set, so the row is read as reference data and the escalation is recorded where the service can record it (DP-03).
read: Architecture v5 slide 8 notes; FSD S8 A2.1.1, A2.2.3.1; TSD S8 T4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and DP-07

impact: A different service level or calendar changes the row and the derived dates only; whether an escalation task is raised in rwb-case is decided later without reopening this read

text: This story's one migration is a step named V2015_1__case_deviation_read.sql in the per-service Flyway sequence of rwb_deviation, and it creates the read-only view v_case_deviation over deviation with one index on (case_id, cleared_at).
why: DP-15 requires one Flyway sequence per service but no source prints a migration file name or a view name for this service; both are design choices that add no business table and no column.

text: The eleven legacy test cases of RWB-E2-015 carry no published level, so each is run at Component level here where it belongs to this single service, and the case-side cases are listed with no criterion here and run at Component level by RWB-P3-E2015-APP, with End to end left to RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-015 section 16 prints System and Access as its level column, and section 16 of the template requires Unit, Component, Contract, Integration, End to end or NFR; a System case that only exercises one service is a Component case in the target.
